blocks.content: Natural vegetation is essential for maintaining the delicate ecological balance, conserving soil moisture, and supporting diverse wildlife habitats across the sub-continent.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Natural vegetation refers to plant communities that grow naturally without human intervention, often termed virgin vegetation.
Forests play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance, controlling soil erosion, and regulating regional climate patterns.
The spatial distribution of natural vegetation in India is primarily determined by variation in precipitation, temperature, altitude, and soil type.
Vegetation provides critical ecosystem services including biodiversity preservation, timber production, and watershed management.
Deforestation, overgrazing, and habitat degradation represent severe threats to indigenous plant cover across the country.

items: The National Forest Policy of 1952 sets the target of maintaining 33% of India's geographical area under forest cover.
Tropical Evergreen Forests occur in regions receiving more than 200 cm of annual rainfall, whereas Deciduous Forests dominate areas with 70 to 200 cm rainfall.
Mangrove forests in coastal deltas serve as vital natural buffers against storm surges, cyclones, and soil erosion.
